# EnVault

> EnVault is a native macOS app for secrets and .env files, with an `envault` command-line tool and an MCP server for AI coding agents. Vaults are end-to-end encrypted and sync through iCloud. Agents can use secrets (run commands with an env file loaded, list variable names, add or rotate keys) without seeing the values; reading a value needs the user's Touch ID approval.

## For AI agents

- Connect over MCP: `claude mcp add envault -- envault mcp` (Claude Code), `codex mcp add envault -- envault mcp` (Codex); other clients: command `envault`, args `["mcp"]`. Tools: status, list_items, list_keys, run_command, set_keys, unset_keys, get_values, scan.
- Or use the shell: `envault ls --json`, `envault keys <project> <item> --json`, `envault run <project> <item> -- <cmd>` (output redacted), `envault set <project> <item> KEY=value` (`KEY=-` reads stdin, `--generate KEY` stores a random secret unseen), `envault unset <project> <item> KEY`.
- Never write secret values into files, code, commits, logs or chat. `envault get`, `pull`, `env` and `run --no-redact` reveal values and ask the user; use them only when asked.
- Exit codes: 1 error, 2 scan found secrets, 3 not found, 4 needs the user (unlock or approve: tell them), 5 refused (don't retry), 64 usage.
- `envault agent-guide` prints these instructions for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md; `envault agent-guide --skill` prints a Claude Code skill.
